newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Six groups vie for $150 mln Manila rail project.
newsitem.headline: Six groups vie for $150 mln Manila rail project.

text.p: Six local and foreign groups have expressed interest in putting up the country's second light rail transit (LRT 2) project, a Light Rail Transit Authority (LRTA) official said on Thursday.
Enrico Garcia, LRT 2 project manager told Reuters the following groups attended the prebidding conference last Wednesday:

Itochu Corp and Hyundai Engineering & Construction Co Ltd ; Kajima Corp and Samsung Corp; Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd, Philippine National Construction Co and Bechtel Corp of the U.S; Hyundai Engineering & Construction Co Ltd ; Marubeni Corp, Balfour of the U.S. and DMCI Holdings Inc ; and D.J. Pumak consortium, a group of Filipino and foreign businessmen.
Garcia said the groups are vying for the construction of the rail transit's substructure and the underground stations estimated to cost $150 million.
Bidding date is scheduled on January 17, 1997. There will be separate biddings for the depot and the trackworks.
The 14-kilometer line will extend from Recto Avenue in Manila to Santolan in suburban Pasig City.
The 26 four-car fully air conditioned trains will be able to ferry 500,000 passengers daily. It is scheduled for commercial operation by the year 2000.
